message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult male individuals. The genes responsible for mane growth (including those controlling hair density and pigmentation) are typically expressed dominantly, meaning that even if a male lion inherits only one copy of the relevant allele from each parent, it will still develop a full mane. This trait is a classic example of dominance in the lion’s genome.
